body: Forward test of the promise-tracker credibility method (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Probability 0.38 (naive base rate 0.50) that: Transrail Lighting FY27 order intake is ≥₹10,000 cr. Evidence: Q2 FY27 call (Nov-2026): order book ₹14,218 cr at 30-Sep-2026, plus ₹1,747 cr declared after quarter-end; MD Randeep Narang: 'confident to achieve an annual order intake of INR10,000-plus crores'; 'Already INR3,500 crores, INR4,000 crores in the bag'; ₹18,000 cr already bid + ~₹30,000 cr more to bid in 5 months at a 10–12% historical win ratio. 'Since listing, we have not missed any of our revenue or margin guidance' (revenue Q2 ₹2,056 cr, +32%; EBITDA margin 11.6%). Reasoning: Arithmetic check: ₹48,000 cr of bids × 10–12% ≈ ₹4,800–5,800 cr more wins → ₹8,300–9,800 cr total, i.e., the target needs above-normal win rates. The clean record is on revenue/margin, not order intake (more lumpy). Lean below base. Resolution: YES if Transrail reports FY27 order intake/inflow (incl. L1 converted to orders within FY27, as the company counts it) ≥₹10,000 cr in its Q4 FY27 presentation, press release or call. Source: Transrail Q4 FY27 investor presentation / earnings call transcript. Resolve by 2027-05-31; score with Brier vs base rate.

Model: worksheet scenarios bear 30%→0.38x, base 45%→0.81x, bull 15%→1.58x with σ=0.40; reverse DCF base-case IRR 7.5%; card rule output: size 0: blocked by Expected value vs hurdle (EV 0.89x anchored (raw 0.74x) vs hurdle 1.76x → below hurdle → size 0). data.base_rate_reasoning: India non-financial, mcap Rs 1,000-20,000 cr at T, 5 yrs from 30-Sep-2016 and 30-Sep-2018 (survivorship-free, dead firms included, stratum-weighted). n=208 company-snapshots (54 distress-census D, 153 live L at weight 5.63, 1 delisted-other X at 4.26); 95% CIs (company bootstrap within stratum): P(>=3x) 14.1-28.7%, P(<=0.5x) 7.0-16.1%, P(blow-up) 10.2-21.4%. Two start dates only, and they disagree (2016: >=3x 16%, blow-up 21%; 2018: 26%, 10%). Price return only (no dividends, ~1%/yr). Blow-up = close <=0.2x the close at T, liquidation or compulsory delisting (no fraud field). Remaining survivorship leak toward FEWER failures (IBBI firms renamed/merged and 221 IBBI rows without identifiers missing; voluntary/merger delistings X under-covered). A survivors-only sample from the same frame says P(<=0.5x) 7% instead of 11%.
